bullets.md: **CI can deploy through the console.** `carlos services create --role deploy --app <a> --rungs canary,edge <name>` mints a credential that can ship, and promote or roll back only the rungs you name: `canary`, `edge` and `beta`, never `stable`. In CI, set `CARLOS_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_CONSOLE` and run `carlos deploy` as usual. The first deploy of a new app still needs a person, because a deploy credential cannot create the app or set up its first host. It cannot hotfix, delete the app, or change retention or domains. `carlos services list` gains a RUNGS column. The CLI refuses to run with both `CARLOS_SERVICE_TOKEN` and `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_BUCKET` or `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_DIR` set.
**A failed rollback says so.** When the console cannot sign a rollback, it now answers "Nothing was rolled back." Before, it said "Nothing was promoted."
**`carlos db` no longer panics.** If `carlos db pull` or `query` could not create its temporary file, the restore crashed. It now reports the error.

**The boxes come back onto the release train.** The flagship boxes have been running a hotfix build of v0.23.0 (f3f6cf73). It carried four fixes. Three are in v0.24.0, and their operator notes are there: a box runs its adopt work on its own loop, lists the bucket by app, and reads in parallel. The fourth is new in this release. When a box cannot stage a release itself, it asks a root pass to do it. That request used to be sent at most once a minute, and one made inside the minute was dropped, so a second release soon after the first waited for the next change to be noticed. On the flagship that was 98 extra seconds. The request is now limited to once every 15 seconds, and one made inside that window is sent at its end instead of dropped. Rolling this release moves those boxes off the hotfix with nothing lost.

**If your boxes are coming from v0.23.0 or a hotfix of it, read v0.24.0's operator notes first.** Its changes now apply to the boxes: the keyless config guard, the box with no deployment store, and alerts to SNS. The check that matters most is this one. Every box that runs placed instances must hold the right `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY` before you roll. A box without it, or with a key that does not open an instance's sealed config, will not wake that instance.

**Leave `CARLOS_HOST_CLAIM` unset on the console.** Any value that is not blank turns it on, including `0` and `false`. The console reads it once, when it starts. Nothing writes host claims yet, so with it on, `carlos db pull` and `carlos db query` fail for every host.

**Do not set `CARLOS_REGION_HA` on a box yet.** It is the switch for multi-box regions, which this release does not finish. Left unset, a box publishes no `region-ha-1` capability and no headroom, and nothing changes.

**Deploy credentials need the console's signing key.** The console signs each deploy promote with a grant limited to the credential's rungs, so the console must hold its release key, as it already does for promotes. It adds a `rungs` column to its `cli_tokens` table when it starts. The change is additive.

**Region HA foundations ship dormant.** Every box's edges file gains `box_id`, which is the box's label. Box bootstrap also creates `/run/carlos/hostguard` and `/data/hostguard`, mode 2770, owned by `carlos:carlos`, when tmpfiles next runs. Nothing uses them yet. The host claim, generation selection and park libraries have no callers, so the boxes behave as before.

**Read the plan before applying the infrastructure modules.** `region-host` gains a termination queue, an EventBridge rule and a box-role policy to read the queue, and its root volume is now deleted when the instance terminates. `deployment-buckets` gains a bucket policy that makes `control/boxes/*` create-only and undeletable. A bucket holds one policy, so check whether yours already has one before you apply. Nothing in this release needs them, so applying can wait. The own-bucket S3 version grants are split into separately named statements, with the same permissions.
**The scanner host fix is in this release too.** It is the freshclam change from v0.24.1.
**Either roll order works.** Nothing in this release needs the console and the boxes to roll in a particular order.

**The scanner host boots.** In v0.24.0, a new `scanner-host` box failed its first boot with `SCANNER-HOST FAILED: first freshclam failed 3 times`. Debian's AppArmor profile only lets freshclam read its own config under `/etc/clamav`, and the boot script gave it a copy elsewhere. It now uses the packaged config. A box from v0.24.0 never opened its port, so nothing was ever scanned through it. Pin `scanner-host` to v0.24.1 and replace the box with `tofu apply -replace=module.<name>.aws_instance.scanner`.

bullets.md: **Canaries have a one-label address, and can be created again.** A canary's host is now `<name>-<app>.<your account>.<apps domain>`, so canary `new-queue` of app `jam` is `new-queue-jam.bab.oncarlos.com`. The old address put a dot between the name and the app. The console refused that, so `carlos canary` could not create a canary for an app that runs a process. The name and the app together can be at most 63 characters. You need this release's CLI.

**Deploys reach running instances sooner on busy boxes.** A box notices a promote sooner, and it restarts an awake instance onto the new release on its own two-second check instead of waiting for the rest of its work. On the flagship, noticing a promote had taken 16 to 43 seconds, and the restart then waited about 48 seconds more.

**An instance never starts without its secrets.** A box that cannot open an instance's sealed secrets no longer wakes it or takes it on. A box that can takes it instead. If none can, it does not start. Before, it could start with none of its config or secrets.

**One address, one app.** `carlos instances create` and `carlos canary` are refused when another app in your account already holds the host, including an app in the Trash, or when the host is a domain attached to another app. Before, both creates succeeded and one of them served nothing.
**Nothing new to type.** The CLI has no new commands or flags in this release.

**Check every box's secrets key before rolling the boxes.** A box now takes an exec instance only if it can open that instance's sealed config. Without `CARLOS_SECRETS_KEY`, or with a key that does not open the config, it does not wake the instance or mint its record. It logs `agent: config guard: refusing <host>` and lists the host under `metrics.config_refusals` in its private snapshot, `status/boxes/<box>.json`. A box that cannot read the deployment store to check refuses too, and asks again after 30 seconds. Instances with no sealed config are not affected.

**A box with no deployment store refuses exec instances.** With `CARLOS_HIBERNATE_BUCKET` set and neither `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_BUCKET` nor `CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_DIR`, a box cannot tell whether an instance's config is sealed, so it refuses. On a deployment with no sealed config at all, set `CARLOS_NO_SEALED_CONFIG=1`. Never set it on a box that serves tenants. The box then logs that the check is bypassed and says so in its snapshot. With a deployment store configured, the setting is ignored.

**Roll the console to this release before pointing it at a scanner host.** An older console records an archive that clamd could only partly scan as infected. This release records it as not scanned, and a scan time-out as failed, so the next sweep tries it again. A real signature match is still infected.

**Object-storage scanning has its own box.** The new `infra/modules/scanner-host` module runs clamd on one box per deployment, reachable only from the console's security group. Set its outputs on the console: `clamd_addr` as `CARLOS_CLAMD_ADDR` and `stream_max_bytes` as `CARLOS_CLAMD_MAX_BYTES`. The console also needs `CARLOS_SCAN_TAG_KEY`, and refuses to boot with an address and no key. Set `store_scanning = true` on the console box's `region-host` so its role can read and tag store objects. It is off by default, and a deployment that leaves it off plans no change. Wiring the engine does not switch scanning on. `carlos system antivirus enable` does. A replaced scanner box gets a new private IP, so update `CARLOS_CLAMD_ADDR` after any `-replace`. Pin modules to v0.24.0: v0.23.0 does not contain `scanner-host`.
**The app regions rollback floor is v0.23.0.** v0.23.0 is the first release that understands app regions. Once any app holds a region other than the home, do not roll the console below v0.23.0.

**Boxes can send alerts to SNS.** Set `CARLOS_ALERT_SNS_TOPIC_ARN` to the box's own region's alerts topic, and anyone subscribed gets each fire and clear by email. The box's instance role needs `sns:Publish` on that topic. The modules in this repo do not grant it. A box with neither this nor `CARLOS_ALERT_WEBHOOK` logs `NO SINK CONFIGURED` when it starts. `carlos status --live` gains a last column: `alerts=sns`, `alerts=webhook`, `alerts=webhook+sns`, `alerts=not-delivered`, or `alerts=sns-unavailable` when a topic is set but the box could not build its SNS client. A dash means the box runs an older release.

**Boxes list the bucket by app.** To find instance records, a box now lists each account's apps and each app's `instances/` prefix, eight requests at a time, instead of every object under `apps/`. If one app's listing fails, the box logs a `provision: listing` line, converges everything it did see, and removes no route on that pass. The agent also logs an `agent: fast converge:` line when a step of its fast loop takes longer than five seconds.
**Either roll order works.** Nothing in this release needs the console and the boxes to roll in a particular order.

bullets.md: **A deploy reaches a running instance in seconds.** When a box adopts a new release, an instance that is awake restarts onto it within a few seconds. Before, it kept serving the old build for about two minutes, longer than `carlos deploy` waits, so a deploy could report a timeout and a restart seemed to be needed. Instances on one box restart one at a time, two seconds apart.

**Static sites show a deploy on the next page load.** Browsers now check with the edge before reusing a page or file from a static site, and get a quick "not modified" answer while nothing has changed. Before, a browser could keep showing the old page for hours or days after a deploy.

**Read a copy of an instance's database.** `carlos db pull --app <a> --out <file>` saves a copy of a sleeping instance's database on your machine, and `carlos db query --app <a> --sql "…"` runs one query against a fresh copy. Both say how recent the copy is. The copy is read-only and never touches the live database. Name an instance with `--instance` when the app has more than one.

**Region flags.** `carlos apps create`, `carlos deploy` and `carlos canary` take `--region`. A console that is not assigning app regions yet says so and starts the app in its home region. `carlos deploy --region` on an existing app stops before shipping if the region differs from the app's own. The line `carlos instances create` prints now names the place the instance runs.
**Invite links ask before you join.** Opening an invite link shows who invited you and a Join button. Nothing happens until you press it.

**Sending domains you did not set up.** If a domain already has a sending identity that your account did not create, `carlos email domains add` asks you to prove you control it: publish a TXT record at `_carlos-mail.<domain>` with the value `carlos-mail-account=<account>`, then add the domain again. A domain another account holds now reads "sending domain unavailable". A claim that is not verified within 7 days can be taken by another account.

**Stores no longer share a bucket by accident.** App and environment names are joined with "-", so app `shop` with environment `eu` and app `shop-eu` used to map to the same bucket. The second one is now refused with a 409, and nothing is created.
**Platform domains.** An operator can attach one of the deployment's own domains to an app with `carlos domains attach --platform`. Members cannot attach, change or detach those names.
**Roll the boxes, then the console.** With the new switches left off, either order is safe. The two switches below need every box on v0.23.0 first.

**Leave `CONSOLE_SECRETS_ENVELOPE_V2` off until every box runs v0.23.0.** When it is on, the console seals new secrets so they open only for their own account and app. A box on an older release cannot open them, and the app's whole config stops updating on that box. Rolling a box back below v0.23.0 after turning it on does the same. A value that is not true or false stops the console from starting.

**v0.23.0 is the first release that understands app regions.** That makes it the rollback floor the README describes: once any app holds a region other than the home, do not roll the console below v0.23.0. `CONSOLE_APP_REGIONS` is off by default. Turn it on only by the README's steps. Boxes now publish `serves_shared_pool`, `accepts_inbound` and, where they hold the secrets key, `secrets_key_fp` in their edges file.

**Boxes restart awake instances when they adopt a release.** The agent checks every two seconds and restarts at most one instance per check. Workers still converge on the old 90-second timer. A restart drains the old process as before: new requests wait for the new one.

**Static responses change their headers.** They now carry `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a weak `ETag` worked out from each file's bytes and type, and no `Last-Modified`. The first request for a file after a deploy reads it once to work out the tag. The edge's own cache still does not store static responses.

**Pin infrastructure modules to v0.23.0.** The box role gains permission to list, read and delete object versions in its own data bucket. Nothing uses it yet, so applying it can wait. Check also that nothing in your policies denies `s3:DeleteObject` on the deployment bucket: purges, store teardown and mail claim release delete objects, and fail without it.

**Run `carlos accounts migrate` with a v0.23.0 CLI.** Pointers are now signed for their account, and migrating re-signs them, which needs the root `CARLOS_RELEASE_KEY`. An older CLI copies them unchanged, and the moved app stops adopting releases.

**Existing data is left in place.** Purging an app now also deletes its tokens, door keys and ledgers, but apps purged before this release keep theirs. Removing a sending domain that was added before this release leaves its SES identity in SES. Moving an app revokes its door keys, so moved apps need new ones.

bullets.md: **Database size on the app Overview.** A new tile shows how much disk your app's databases use, including copies that are asleep.

**Busy and large instances can finish a move.** An instance that is awake and writing, or that keeps large database files, can now finish moving to another region. Before, such a move could wait in `preparing` and never become ready. The cut still copies everything that is left, exactly, before the instance serves from its new region.
**Nothing new to type.** The CLI has no new commands or flags in this release.
**v0.22.1 was tagged but never published.** v0.22.2 supersedes it, so roll v0.22.2 and pin modules to v0.22.2.

**A move becomes ready when little is left to copy.** By default, a preparing round now promotes when it copied 16 MiB or less. To change that bar, set `CARLOS_MOVE_READY_DELTA_BYTES` in `/etc/carlos/host.env`; the agent reads it when it starts. `0` restores the old rule that a round must copy nothing. A value that is not a whole number of bytes is ignored with a log line, and the default stays. The ready log line now shows the bytes copied, the number of changes and the bar.

**Copy receipts in the source box's data bucket.** A box moving an instance away keeps receipts at `move-receipts/<host>.json` in its own data bucket, so large objects that have not changed are not copied again. The cut and an abort delete them. A deployment whose data-bucket policy denies DeleteObject keeps stale receipts, which are harmless. The box policy in this repo already allows the prefix.

**The cut is still exact.** It copies everything that is left before it flips the record. If an object changes during that final copy, the cut waits for the next pass instead of landing an incomplete copy.

**The Database tile is console only.** It reads the database sizes boxes have reported since v0.21.0, so it needs no box roll and no env or IAM change. A slow read shows a dash and never holds up the page.

bullets.md: **Availability, apart from errors.** `carlos availability` lists the requests an app's instances could not answer, every 502, 503 and 504 the edge saw, grouped by cause instead of by page. One outage is one row, however many pages it hit. `--fp <id>` expands a cause to each request and the path it asked for. The same view is the new Availability tab beside Errors.
**Errors is shorter.** `carlos errors` and the Errors tab keep the app's own 500s and the error lines in its logs. Edge 502s, 503s and 504s, failed wakes and exits have moved to Availability.

**Replica instances.** `carlos instances create --role replica --region <r>` makes a second instance of an app, holding a one-way copy of the live instance's data, in a region near its buyers. The live instance names the regions it allows replicas in with `--replicas ie,uk` when it is created. Until a batch of orders drains home, a replica holds order data in its own region, so the regions are always a decision on the live instance, never a default.

**Door keys.** `carlos instances door-key create`, `list` and `revoke` manage keys for the edge-local door. That is one socket on a box that a process running beside an app's instances can dial to reach any of them, whether it is asleep, moved to another box or awake. A key is shown once, when it is created. The door is off until the box's operator turns it on.
**Faster log reads.** Log chunks are now fetched 16 at a time instead of one by one, which speeds up `carlos logs`, Errors and Availability.
**A restored app keeps its pipeline.** When the console registers an app whose files are already in the bucket, it keeps that app's release pipeline instead of resetting it to the default.

**Roll the console first, then the boxes, close together.** The boxes record why the edge had no answer and the console shows it. A console on its own groups stored 502s under "cause not recorded", and new ones too until the boxes roll. Boxes on their own, under an old console, list each cause as its own row on Errors. Rolling the console back is safe: nothing in the bucket is rewritten.

**A new CLI against an old console.** `carlos availability` fails with `not found: check --account and --app, and that your token's address is a member`. Until the console rolls, that message means the console predates the command, not that the app or your membership is missing. An old console silently ignores `carlos instances create --role replica` and creates an ordinary instance in that region instead.

**No replicas until every box has rolled.** Only this release keeps replicas out of DNS latency routing. Each box adds two columns to its registry when it starts (`routes.replicas` and `routes.replica`). There is nothing to migrate, and a box rolled back ignores them.

**Long polls show up in Availability.** A visitor who gives up after waiting five seconds or more, before the instance has sent response headers, is filed as an outage. On a sleeping route the five seconds include the wake. An endpoint that holds its headers longer by design, like a long poll, shows a standing row, and that row is expected. A visitor who leaves sooner is no longer filed at all, so expect fewer one-off 502s on static files.
**Tunnelled failures are filed once.** On a route a box reaches over a tunnel or a fleet, the front box files only its own hop failures, and the box serving the app files the rest.

**Instance moves.** A box cutting a move now fences the instance so a scheduled wake cannot start it again mid-move. A move past ready can no longer be aborted, and a replica cannot be moved: delete it and create one in the new region. A later release's boxes rely on this console's abort rule, which is one more reason to roll the console first.

**The edge-local door is off by default.** It stays off until a box sets `CARLOS_EDGE_DOOR=/run/carlos/edge-local.sock` and its agent restarts. The calling process's user must also be enrolled with `carlos bootstrap --socket-consumer <user>`. The console re-signs door keys every 12 hours, and a key whose record has not been re-signed for 72 hours stops working, so a console down that long closes every door.

**Each instance gets its own `/dev/shm`.** Instance units no longer see the host's `/dev/shm`, so an instance cannot reach another's shared memory. They also no longer set `RestrictSUIDSGID=`, which broke `openat2` on systemd 257 and kept the isolated exec probe from reporting ready. `carlos system update` installs the new units, and a running instance picks them up when it next restarts.

Edges also learn which box serves a new host within about 30 seconds, down from as much as six minutes.

bullets.md: **Named deploy destinations.** `carlos config destinations` keeps the places an app deploys to in `.carlos/config`, and `carlos deploy -d <name>` picks one.
**Sidecars.** `carlos sidecars` runs a process beside each enrolled member of an app, such as a document converter. it takes enable, create, ls, wake, rm and logs.

**Email you can follow.** `carlos email events` shows what happened to each message an app sent (delivered, bounced, complained about or delayed) for 30 days. `carlos email events push` posts those events to the app itself, signed. `carlos email domains rm` stops an app sending from a domain and frees the domain for another account once no app uses it.

**A store per environment.** `carlos store create --environment <e>` gives one named environment its own bucket and credential, delivered into that environment's config. an app can now have each instance get its own environment and store.

**Purge every host of an account at once.** `Carlos-Purge-Host` now takes a list of up to 32 hosts, each checked against the same app and account. a host the box doesn't serve is skipped. The control socket's `POST /purge` takes `{"path":"*"}` to clear the whole host.

notes.md:
#### Region residence: instances know where they live, and can move

This release is about placement. Three pieces land together (platform #329, #331, #346):

- **Armed-placement validation on instance create** (#329). Creating an instance names a region, and the console now refuses a code that is not armed on the deployment instead of provisioning into nowhere. Each box's `edges` file publishes its own placement code, and every exec child inherits it as `CARLOS_REGION`, so an app can tell where it is running without asking anyone.
- **Two-phase, data-following instance moves** (#331). `POST .../instances/{host}/move` requests a move to another armed region; the host prepares in rounds, mirroring the instance's replica prefix into the destination's staging bucket until the copy is current; `POST .../move/cut` then cuts over, with a re-checkpoint at the cut so nothing written in the gap is lost. `DELETE .../move` aborts cleanly at either phase. Staging wins over a stale local copy, a failed fallback is a hard fail rather than a silent downgrade, and a serial nudge on every box-side write means the cut chain converges in seconds rather than five-minute hops.
- **The armed-regions endpoint** (#346). `GET /api/cli/apps/{account}/{app}/regions` returns the deployment's regions with their `armed` state, the home region's name, and the default, so pickers in the console, the CLI, and consumer apps draw from one list.

#### Also in this release

- **`served_by` on instances** (#337): an instance row now carries where it is *observed* to be served (the edges that actually join it), beside where it was *placed*.
- **Control and edges files carry placement + data-bucket coordinates**, so a box and its peers can locate each other's replica prefixes without a console round trip.
- **`sibling_staging_arns`** on the `region-remote-host` and region-host Terraform modules: the push-only `moves/*` grant that lets a host stage into a sibling region's bucket and nothing else.
- **`carlos-app@` units can no longer reach IMDS** (#351/#352); a `host_role` drop-in re-opens it for the apps that need instance credentials.

The operator CLI verbs are unchanged from v0.16.0; the new surface is on the console API and in the host, edge, and activator halves of the same binary.

#### carlos features — app feature flags on the deployment object

The headline: `carlos features set` and `carlos features list` (platform #347, PR #350). An app's own feature flags — switches the app defines, the platform stores, serves and audits, but never interprets:

```sh
carlos features set --app titogo sandbox=on

`key=` with nothing after the equals clears a key. The documented face of every carlos command now says `--app`. Both spellings have always parsed identically — Go's flag package treats `-app` and `--app` the same — so this release changes what the tool teaches, not what it accepts: usage pages, docs, and error messages all show the double-dash form, and the four flags you type all day gain short aliases:

notes.md:
#### carlos economics backhaul

What serving through region edges costs the platform. When a request lands on a region edge and is carried on to the account's home box, the inter-region leg is a cost the platform absorbs — it sits inside the account's egress total, never on top of it, and appears in nobody's bill. This verb is the operator's view of that leg:

```
carlos economics backhaul [-period mtd|last|7d]
```

Per account: bytes backhauled, the share of that account's egress it represents, and what the leg comes to at the rate card's inter-region $/GB. The header shows the period's coverage (days of meters present) so a partial month reads as one. Backhaul meters are a subset of the egress meters and are never counted as usage. Operator only — a non-operator's token gets the same bare 404 an unknown route gets. (#288, #284)

`carlos economics` with no sub-verb now lists both `bill` and `backhaul`.

#### Multi-region ingress, hardened

The same binary is the edge and the host agent, so this tag also carries the steering work that has been rolling out across the fleet:

- **Custom domains through any edge** (#287): the edges file publishes attached custom domains under their own names, aliases are marked on the wire, routes win collisions, and the config layer denies entry for names that must not be published.
- **Wildcard parents** (#300, #290): derived from the deployment's hosts — provisioned routes as well as console-minted ones — with the class mark on the wire, a serialized refresh, and an async wake that is blind to catch-alls.
- **Per-box domain health stamps** (#303, #304): run on every box again, once per tick, never on a fleet box, inert without an apps domain; a resolver failure never overwrites a DNS verdict.
- **Certificate backfill** (#291, #297): the issuer backfills pre-existing certificates into `control/certs/`, with the settled stamp pinned on the bucket side.
- **Domains reconcile is a housekeeper duty** (#289): one writer per deployment.
- **Snapshot fingerprint** ignores the box's own scheduling stamps (#207), ending a churn where every tick looked like a change.

#### Docs

Two docs sites (carlosframework.com/docs, carloku.com/docs) now build from a corpus in this repo, with a gate that holds the CLI reference to `main.go`'s dispatch switch — every command must have a page, every fence a language, every link a target.

notes.md:
#### A static site gets a URL from the CLI alone

`carlos deploy -kind static` with no `-host` now mints the app's own platform hostname — `<app>.<sqid>.<apps-domain>` — and the static route record that serves it. Publishing a site no longer requires owning a domain or pointing DNS at anything:

```
carlos apps create -app mysite
carlos deploy -kind static ./dist
```

Everything it needs was already there: DNS under the apps domain resolves to the edge at any depth, and the edge derives its own per-account wildcard certificate from the live route table. The missing piece was a record, and now the CLI writes one.

`-host` still does exactly what it did — it now means "serve on this hostname instead of the app's own", and remains the answer for a domain you control.

#### carlos instances set-channel

The only door onto which release channel a route follows. A route's channel lives in its instance record, which the box converges from every pass, so `carlos route -channel` on a box is reverted within seconds — and until now nothing else could change it. A route that landed on the wrong channel had a URL that served nothing and no way back.

```
carlos instances set-channel -app <a> -host <h> -channel <c>
```

A move must clear the rules of **both** channels it touches, each at its strictest, because a move can achieve a promotion: with `production` requiring approvals and `edge` requiring none, moving the production route onto edge would otherwise serve unreviewed code from a guarded URL with nobody's approval. Gated moves are proposed and confirmed in the console, exactly like a promote.

#### carlos instances create -kind

`instance` (default) | `service` | `static` — exposing the route class the record shape has always carried.

#### carlos schedule

Recurring and one-shot work per app, owned by the platform rather than by a
box's crontab: `carlos schedule ls | set | rm | run`. Landed in #285 and
included in this tag; boxes and consoles are already rolled for it.

notes.md:
#### Tenant email — `carlos email`

An app on CARLOS can now send mail without running an MTA or holding a cloud key. The platform mints a sending identity, publishes DKIM, SPF and DMARC where it owns the zone, and delivers working SMTP credentials as config.

```
carlos email enable -app <app>
```

That is the whole walk: declare, provision the domain, wait for verification, deliver. The identity defaults to the app's own host, so the signing domain matches the domain of the links inside the mail. Credentials arrive as `CARLOS_SMTP_HOST`, `_PORT`, `_USER`, `_PASS`, `_FROM` (rename the set with `-env-prefix`). Transport is submission on 587 with STARTTLS.

For a customer's own domain, `-domain mail.example.com` prints the record set for the zone's owner to publish and polls until SES confirms it.

The rest of the surface:

| Verb | What it does |
|---|---|
| `carlos email status` | What is declared, which domains verified, what was delivered |
| `carlos email test -to <addr>` | Sends a real message through a throwaway credential, then revokes it |
| `carlos email domains add` | Add a second sending domain |
| `carlos email credentials create\|list\|revoke` | Standalone credentials for something not on CARLOS; the password is shown once |
| `carlos email rotate [-finish]` | Two-phase key rotation |
| `carlos email pause\|resume` | A deployment operator's abuse brake |

##### Three things worth knowing

- **A freshly minted credential does not work for the first minute or two.** SES's SMTP endpoint does not see a new IAM access key immediately, and the symptom is `535 Authentication Credentials Invalid` — which reads exactly like a wrong password and is not one. `carlos email test` now waits this out; an app's own first sends after `enable` will still meet it.
- **DMARC passes on the DKIM rail alone.** Records are published with `adkim=s; aspf=s`, and that strictness is what stops one tenant's signature authenticating another tenant's From address on a shared domain. SPF authenticates but does not *align*, because the envelope sender is a region-qualified subdomain. So never turn off DKIM signing on a sending identity, and treat `p=reject` as safe but unforgiving.
- **The MAIL FROM subdomain carries its region forever**, fixed at first verification. On a custom domain it lives in the customer's zone — the one record CARLOS cannot republish for them.

#### Also in this release

- **Multi-region steering** is member-settable and pool-railed.
- `carlos email status` names a verified domain that emits no SES events, rather than showing counts that can only ever be zero.

notes.md:
#### Windows

`carlos` now runs on Windows as a **client**: `carlos login`, `ship`, `deploy`,
`logs` — everything that talks to a console or a bucket — from a Windows
workstation against a Linux fleet. Download `carlos-windows-amd64.zip` (or
`-arm64`), unpack `carlos.exe` onto your `PATH`, and check it against
`SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Two things to know:

- **`carlos update` does not self-replace on Windows.** Windows cannot rename a
  new binary over a running `.exe`, so `carlos update` tells you when you're
  behind and hands you the zip URL instead of swapping itself.
- **Your credentials file is not permission-protected on Windows.** On Linux and
  macOS `~/.carlos/credentials` is written `0600`; the equivalent mode means
  nothing on `%USERPROFILE%\.carlos\credentials`. Don't `carlos login` on a
  shared machine.

Windows cannot BE a box — `carlos agent` and the root-side passes need unix
sockets, `flock` and systemd, and refuse there rather than pretending.

105 commits since v0.9.0, including:

- **Service principals** (#227) — non-human members that deploy.
- **Edge response compression** (#224, #230) — gzip on the shared edge.
- **Logs terminal pane** (#209) in the console.

  (#211, #214, #213).

notes.md:
The proactive release: when `carlos` can see both the problem and the fix, it offers the fix (platform#160, #161, #162).

- **Moved consoles are explained, not numbered**: a permanently-redirected console produces `this console has moved: old -> new`, an offer to log in to the new home, and an offer to repoint your `.carlos/config` — never again "unexpected response (status 308)". Redirects are never silently followed (a cross-host follow used to drop your credentials into a mystery 401).
- **Missing logins are offered**: run any command while logged out and, at a terminal, the CLI runs the login right there and then continues your command. Scripts keep the exact errors they've always matched.
- **`carlos update`**: a once-a-day muted hint when a newer release exists, and a verb that updates a plain-binary install after verifying the release's signed checksum list (ed25519 key embedded in the binary) — brew and apt installs are handed to their package manager. `update_check: "off"` in `.carlos/config` or `CARLOS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` opts out.

This release introduces `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig`: the checksum list is signed with the CARLOS CLI-update key from here on.

notes.md:
#### carlos deploy — seconds to live

One command from working tree to serving URL: `carlos deploy -app <a> <binary-or-site-dir>` ships, promotes to the channel your instances follow, and waits until the URL provably serves the new build (the edge's new `X-Carlos-Version` header, required over 2xx — exit 0 means live). `-version` defaults to your git short HEAD. On a bake-held production channel it ships, promotes, prints the hold, and exits without waiting — never a bake bypass.

Platform-side (live on CARLOS deployments running ≥ 1fba18f): promotes converge in seconds on every non-baking channel, warm instances restart onto the new build automatically, and brand-new instances stage at first request instead of 503ing.

Also in this release (from #107): `carlos releases`, version targets (`carlos version target`), `-label`/`-notes` on ship, and semver tags cut when a release reaches stable.

**New: Debian packages** — `carlos_0.5.0_{amd64,arm64}.deb`; install with `sudo apt install ./carlos_0.5.0_arm64.deb`. Homebrew: `brew install carlosframework/tap/carlos`.

`carlos` v0.4.0 — the CARLOS platform binary (edge, host agent, operator CLI). Built from carlosframework/platform @ v0.4.0. Verify with SHA256SUMS.txt. See the README for install instructions.

**Supersedes v0.3.0**, which was built from a commit predating the console-API CLI merge.

The headline: **deploys need no bucket access and no keys in the terminal.**

```
carlos auth login -console https://<your-deployment-console>
carlos ship    -account <acct> -app <app> -version <sha> ./<binary>
carlos promote -account <acct> -app <app> <sha> canary/<name>
```

A logged-in terminal ships and promotes through the console API; the console signs server-side and your account membership is the authorization. `channels` and `rollback` work the same way. The direct bucket mode (`CARLOS_DEPLOYMENT_BUCKET` + signing key, root or scoped) remains for operators and CI, and `promote -hotfix` is deliberately operator-only.

Also since v0.3.0: host & process monitoring, external-socket advisory, open-ledgers primitive, follow-up hardening.
